summary: 堤坝与河道整治可能让洪水更快涌向下游。欧洲多地开始给河流腾出空间，借洪泛平原、湿地和城市蓄水设施减慢径流。
logic: 束窄河道加剧下游洪峰

paragraphs.brief: 高堤快排难以根治洪水
sentences: Recently, winter floods on the rivers of central Europe have been among the worst for 600 to 700 years, and dams and dykes (protective sea walls) have failed to solve the problem.
最近中欧河流发生的冬季洪水，是六七百年来最严重的几次之一，水坝和防护堤仍未能解决问题。
Traditionally, river engineers have tried to get rid of the water quickly, draining it off the land and down to the sea in rivers reengineered as high-performance drains.
传统上，河流工程师力求快速排水：先让积水离开陆地，再通过被改造成高效排水渠的河道直排入海。
But however high they build the artificial riverbanks, the floods keep coming back.
但不管人工河堤筑得多高，洪水还是会卷土重来。
And when they come, they seem to be worse than ever.
洪水再次到来时，情形似乎比以往更严重。
paragraphs.gist: 中欧近年冬季洪水之重为数百年少见，传统工程把河流改成快速排水通道、不断加高堤防，却未能阻止洪水反复甚至加剧。

paragraphs.brief: 复原河湾漫滩以缓和洪峰
sentences: Engineers are now turning to a different plan: to sap the water’s destructive strength by dispersing it into fields, forgotten lakes and flood plains.
如今工程师转向另一套方案，把洪水分散到农田、被遗忘的湖泊和洪泛平原上，以削弱其破坏力。
They are reviving river bends and marshes to curb the flow, and even plugging city drains to encourage floodwater to use other means to go underground.
他们恢复河湾和沼泽以减缓水流，甚至封堵一些城市排水口，引导洪水经其他途径渗入地下。

Back in the days when rivers took a winding path to the sea, floodwaters lost force and volume while meandering across flood plains and inland deltas, but today the water tends to have a direct passage to the sea.
过去，河流蜿蜒入海，洪水曲折地经过洪泛平原和内陆三角洲时，水势和水量都会减小；如今水流往往直奔海洋。
This means that, when it rains in the uplands, the water comes down all at once.
这意味着，一旦高地下雨，雨水就会集中涌向下游。
paragraphs.gist: 工程师转而恢复河湾、湿地与泛滥平原，让水分散、渗入地下并逐渐消耗力量，避免上游降雨经笔直河道同时抵达下游。

paragraphs.brief: 河道工程加剧下游洪灾
sentences: Worse, when the flood plains are closed off, the river’s flow downstream becomes more violent and uncontrollable; by turning complex river systems into the simple mechanics of a water pipe, engineers have often created danger where they promised safety.
更糟的是，洪泛平原被隔断后，下游水流更凶猛、更难控制。工程师把复杂的河流系统简化成排水管，原本承诺带来安全，往往反而制造了风险。
The Rhine, Europe’s most engineered river, is a good example.
欧洲受工程改造最深的河流莱茵河就是一个例子。
For a long time engineers have erased its backwaters and cut it off from its plain.
长期以来，工程师填除了回水区，切断了河道与洪泛平原的联系。
The aim was partly to improve navigation, and partly to speed floodwaters out of the Alps and down to the North Sea.
目的既是改善通航，也是让阿尔卑斯山区的洪水加速排入北海。

Now, when it rains in the Alps, the peak flows from several branches of the Rhine coincide where once they arrived separately, and with four-fifths of the Lower Rhine’s flood plain barricaded off, the waters rise.
以前莱茵河各支流的洪峰先后到达，如今阿尔卑斯山区下雨时，洪峰却同时抵达，而莱茵河下游五分之四的洪泛平原已被堤坝隔断，水位因而上涨。
The result is more frequent flooding and greater damage.
其结果是洪水更频繁，破坏更大。
The same thing has happened in the US on the Mississippi River, which drains the world’s second-largest river catchment into the Gulf of Mexico.
美国密西西比河也发生了同样的事，这条河把世界第二大流域的水汇入墨西哥湾。
Despite some $7 billion spent over the last century on levees (embankments), the situation is growing worse.
尽管过去一个世纪已花约70亿美元修建堤防，情况仍在恶化。
paragraphs.gist: 莱茵河被截直、与漫滩隔开后，多条支流的洪峰同时抵达；密西西比河也显示，巨额筑堤投资并不必然减少洪灾。

paragraphs.brief: 英国与奥地利的蓄洪修复
sentences: Specialists in water control now say that a new approach is needed — one which takes the whole landscape into consideration.
治水专家现在认为，需要一种将整个地貌纳入考虑的新办法。
To help keep London’s feet dry, the UK Environment Agency is reflooding 10 square kilometres of the ancient flood plain of the River Thames outside Oxford.
为了让伦敦免遭洪涝，英国环境署正让洪水重新漫入牛津城外泰晤士河沿岸10平方公里的古老洪泛平原。
Nearer to London, it has spent £100 million creating new wetlands and a relief channel across 16 kilometres of flood plain.
在较靠近伦敦的地方，该机构花费 1 亿英镑，在绵延 16 公里的洪泛平原上新建湿地和一条分洪渠。
Similar ideas are being tested in Austria, in one of Europe’s largest river restorations to date.
类似的想法正在奥地利进行试验，这是迄今为止欧洲最大的河流修复之一。

The engineers calculate that the restored flood plain of the Drava River can now store up to 10 million cubic metres of floodwater, and slow down storm surges coming out of the Alps by more than an hour, protecting towns not only in Austria, but as far downstream as Slovenia and Croatia.
工程师估算，修复后的德拉瓦河洪泛平原如今可容纳多达一千万立方米洪水，并使来自阿尔卑斯山区的暴雨洪峰延缓一个多小时，保护的城镇从奥地利一直延伸到下游的斯洛文尼亚和克罗地亚。
paragraphs.gist: 英国在泰晤士河沿岸恢复漫滩和湿地，奥地利德拉瓦河修复工程则用蓄洪空间延缓洪峰，保护范围延伸到更下游的邻国。

paragraphs.brief: 荷兰让部分土地重新受淹
sentences: The Dutch, for whom preventing floods is a matter of survival, have gone furthest.
在荷兰，防洪关乎生存，荷兰人也在这些新做法上走得最远。
This nation, built largely on drained marshes and seabed, has had several severe shocks in the last two decades, when very large numbers of people have had to be evacuated.
这个国家大部分建在排水造地的沼泽和海床上，过去二十年里数度遭受严重水患，大量居民被迫撤离。
Since that time, the Dutch have broken one of their most enduring national stereotypes by allowing engineers to punch holes in dykes.
此后，荷兰人打破了自己长久以来给人留下的固守堤坝的印象，允许工程师在堤上开口。
They plan to return up to a sixth of the country to its former waterlogged state in order to better protect the rest.
他们计划让最多六分之一的国土恢复往日水泽状态，以便更好地保护其余地区。
paragraphs.gist: 荷兰在大规模疏散事件后重新考虑一味封堵洪水的方式，允许在堤坝开口，计划让部分国土重新积水，以保护其余地区。

paragraphs.brief: 柏林建设可渗透的城市
sentences: Water use in cities also needs to change.
城市用水情况也需要改变。
At the moment, cities seem to create floods; they are concreted and paved so that rains flow quickly into rivers.
目前的城市建设似乎反而加剧了洪水：大面积混凝土和硬化路面使雨水迅速流入河流。
A new breed of ‘soft engineers’ wants cities to be porous; Berlin is one place where this is being done.
新一代主张“软工程”的工程师希望让城市地表可以渗水，柏林已经开始这样做。
Tough new rules for new developments mean that drains will be prevented from becoming overloaded after heavy rains.
严格的新开发规定要求，暴雨后排水管网也不能超负荷。

Architects of new urban buildings are diverting rainwater from the roofs for use in toilets and the irrigation of roof gardens, while water falling onto the ground is collected in ponds, or passes underground through porous paving.
设计新建筑时，建筑师把屋面雨水引去冲厕所或浇灌屋顶花园；落在地面的雨水则汇入池塘，或经透水铺装渗入地下。
One high-tech urban development can store a sixth of its annual rainfall, and reuse most of the rest.
其中一个采用新技术的城市开发区可储存全年降雨量的六分之一，其余大部分也可回收利用。
paragraphs.gist: 柏林通过建设规范鼓励屋顶雨水再利用、池塘蓄水和透水铺装，让城市吸收雨水，减轻暴雨时的排水负荷。

paragraphs.brief: 洛杉矶把洪水转化为水源
sentences: Could this be expanded to protect a whole city?
能否扩大这个范围以保护整个城市？
The test case could be Los Angeles.
洛杉矶可能成为检验这种做法的案例。
With non-porous surfaces covering 70% of the city, drainage is a huge challenge.
该市70%的地面不透水，排水是一项艰巨的挑战。
Billions of dollars have been spent digging huge drains and concreting riverbeds, but many communities still flood regularly.
当地已花数十亿美元挖大型排水渠、用混凝土铺砌河床，但许多社区仍经常积水成灾。
Meanwhile, this desert city ships water from hundreds of kilometres away to fill its taps and swimming pool.
与此同时，这座沙漠城市却要从数百公里外调水，供应水龙头和游泳池。
Los Angeles has recently launched a new scheme to utilise floodwater in the Sun Valley section of the city.
洛杉矶最近在市内太阳谷地区推出利用洪水的新计划。
The plan is to catch the rain that falls on thousands of driveways, parking lots and rooftops in the valley.
计划收集落在谷内数千条车道、停车场和屋顶上的雨水。

Trees will soak up water from parking lots; houses and public buildings will capture roof water to irrigate gardens and parks, and road drains will empty into old gravel pits to recharge the city’s underground water reserves.
停车场的积水由树木吸收，住宅和公共建筑收集屋面雨水浇灌花园和公园，道路排水则引入旧砾石坑，补充城市地下水储备。
Result: less flooding and more water for the city.
这样，洪水会减少，城市可用水量会增加。
It may sound expensive, until we realise how much is spent trying to drain cities and protect areas from flooding, and how little this method achieves.
这种做法听起来也许昂贵，但不妨想想城市现在为排水防洪花了多少钱，又取得了多么有限的效果。
paragraphs.gist: 洛杉矶太阳谷计划从停车场、屋顶和道路收集雨水，灌溉绿地并回补地下水，在降低洪灾风险的同时增加本地水源。

items.en: how legislation has forced building designers to improve water use
items.zh: 立法如何迫使建筑设计师改善用水情况
items.why: “tough new rules (严格的新规)”即立法/法规，直接推动建筑师采用收集与再利用雨水等做法。

items.en: two reasons why one river was isolated from its flood plain
items.zh: 一条河流与其漫滩被人为隔开的两个原因。
items.why: 把这条河与洪泛平原隔开有两个目标：改善通航，并让洪水更快流出阿尔卑斯山区到达北海。

items.en: how natural watercourses in the past assisted flood control
items.zh: 自然水道过去如何协助控制洪水
items.why: 旧河道蜿蜒经过洪泛平原与内陆三角洲，洪水在途中减弱、流量减少，有助控制洪势。

items.en: an example of flood control on one river, affecting three countries
items.zh: 一条河流的防洪工程影响三个国家的例子。
items.why: 同一条河的治理让下游奥地利 /斯洛文尼亚/克罗地亚三国受益，满足题意。

items.en: a country which has partly destroyed one of its most typical features in order to control water
items.zh: 一个为了治水而部分拆除本国标志性设施的国家。
items.why: 荷兰以堤坝著称，如今打孔堤坝、恢复被水济的地带，等于部分“破坏”典型国土特征来控水。

items.en: the writer’s comment on the comparative cost-effectiveness of traditional flood control and newer methods
items.zh: 作者对传统洪水控制和较新方法的相对成本效益的评论
items.why: 表面看贵，但与长期巨额排水工程相比更划算/更有效，这是明确的成本效益比较。

items.en: According to the article, which TWO of these statements are true of the new approach to flood control?
items.zh: 根据文章，下列哪两项正确描述了新的防洪办法？
correct: It aims to slow the movement of water to the sea.
其目的是减缓水向海洋的移动。
It will involve the loss of some areas of land.
这将涉及失去一些土地。

items.en: Some of the most severe floods for many centuries have recently occurred in parts of ________.
items.zh: 近来，________的部分地区发生了数百年来最严重的几场洪水。
items.why: 直接给出“central Europe”。(不超过两词)

items.en: The Rhine and the ________ river have experienced similar problems with water control.
items.zh: 莱茵河与________河在治水方面面临过类似的问题。
items.why: 回到对应内容“美国密西西比河也发生了同样的事，这条河把世界第二大流域的水汇入墨西哥湾”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: An area near Oxford will be flooded to protect the city of ________.
items.zh: 为了保护________这座城市，牛津附近的一片区域将用于蓄洪。

items.en: Planners who wish to allow water to pass more freely through city surfaces are called ________.
items.zh: 主张让水更容易渗过城市地表的规划者被称为________。
items.why: 直接同义替换题，取短语原词。
items.solution: 主张采用软性治水措施的工程师

items.en: A proposal for part of the city of ________ could show whether small-scale water projects could be applied on a large scale.
items.zh: 针对________市部分地区的一项提案，有望检验小型治水项目能否推广到更大范围。
items.why: 以洛杉矶“Sun Valley” 片区为试点，检验能否推广至全城。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

pairs: 题干问的是法规产生的影响，原文从针对新开发项目的严格规定讲起。
谈论洪水强度时，severe 的最高程度可以用 worst 表达。
题干的“在牛津附近”对应原文的“在牛津城外”。
points: 把这条河与洪泛平原隔开有两个目标：改善通航，并让洪水更快流出阿尔卑斯山区到达北海。
回到对应内容“美国密西西比河也发生了同样的事，这条河把世界第二大流域的水汇入墨西哥湾”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: Back in the days when rivers took a winding path to the sea, floodwaters lost force and volume …, but today the water tends to have a direct passage to the sea.
连接词 while 引出“while meandering across flood plains and inland deltas”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
Now, when it rains in the Alps, the peak flows from several branches of the Rhine coincide …, the waters rise.
连接词 once 引出“where once they arrived separately, and with four-fifths of the Lower Rhine’s flood plain barricaded off”，说明主句的时间关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 once 把这一层关系补进去。
vocabulary: 暴风雨造成的水位骤涨
